text:
noah: Heads up — hit a weird auth/rotation issue trying to onboard on Windows + Docker Compose. Sample app kept using the old project key after I exported the new one.

rachel: did you set env in the compose file or your host shell? windows + docker can be funky with env propagation.

noah: I set it in docker-compose.override.yml and did `docker compose up --build`. Steps: rotate key in console -> update compose override -> `docker compose up -d` -> container logs show 401s. Debug shows resolver picked up `~/.redwood/creds` inside container with old token.

cli-bot: quick check: are you mounting a host volume that contains stale creds? Common pattern: developers mount ~/.redwood to /home/app/.redwood for local dev. That will pin the old creds file inside the container.

noah: aha yes we mount home dir for convenience. But I updated env only in compose, not the creds file. I expected env to override the creds file.

engzad: parity note: Node SDK precedence historically: 1) in-memory cached creds 2) creds file 3) env vars. Python SDK is env-first. That mismatch is the real footgun here. We should make precedence consistent: env > file > cache, and clear cache on env change.

pm-lina: (typo) pm-lina: This hit a new user during a sales demo too — embarassing. We need a clear onboarding note and a sample-compose that's safe by default (no host mounts, explicit env).

noah: workaround that worked: add `environment:
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY=proj_live_new_zzz` to the service and remove the volume mount to ~/.redwood OR run `docker compose restart` after updating the file.

engzad: proposed fixes: 1) normalize env var names across SDKs to REDWOOD_API_KEY (deprecate REDWOOD_TOKEN with logged warnings) 2) make resolvers always check process.env per-request and invalidate disk-cached creds when env var differs 3) emit a loud startup warning if both env and creds file exist and the masked values mismatch 4) update sampleapps and quickstarts (Docker, Compose, Windows notes) to avoid mounting host creds.

cli-bot: actionable: filed issue redwood/sdk-cred#678 with repro steps and suggested patch. Tagging @eng-runtime.

noah: I also added a tiny troubleshooting snippet to the sampleapp README: `# If you have stale creds mounted into containers, either remove the mount or set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your compose file and restart the container.`

rachel: Small UX ask: CLI should warn when writing creds to disk in a path that is commonly mounted into containers (detect HOME mounting patterns) and suggest `--no-write` or `--output-env` so users can prefer env-based rotation in container workflows.

engzad: Good call. Also add a CI test in sampleapp that runs under docker-compose: start with old creds file, rotate by changing env, then assert subsequent request uses new key. This would catch regressions.

pm-lina: I'll update onboarding checklist: replace examples that show `mount: ~/.redwood` with a note and safe alternative using `env_file` or CI secrets. Add migration doc: "If you see 401s after rotation, check mounted creds and restart containers."

noah: thanks — resolved for now. Workaround is to remove mount + restart. Will follow up with PR for README and the repro script in the issue.

rachel: thanks — let's also make the logged warning mask tokens but show last 4 chars so users can confirm mismatch without exposing secrets.

engzad: agreed. Scope: patch the resolver (node + python) to env-first, clear cache on mismatch, add startup mismatch warning, add docker-compose sample update, and add CI test. Target milestone: 1.9.1.

cli-bot: Reminder: please link PRs to issue redwood/sdk-cred#678 and ping @devex for docs review.
